stories.title: lld-skill: Low-level design plugin for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, Cursor...): classes, APIs, patterns, concurrency, tests. Built from per-lesson analysis of the InterviewReady LLD course; benchmarked blind against other LLD skills
stories.body:
Low-level design for coding agents. Classes, APIs, data structures, design patterns, concurrency and tests, decided the way Gaurav Sen's free InterviewReady Low Level Design course teaches them. Works in your real codebase and in interviews.

Most "design patterns" prompts make agents reach for patterns. This one makes them do what the course does: find the concrete problem first, pick the tool that removes it, say which option was rejected and why, and get correctness and thread safety right before extensibility. Benchmark

lld was compared blind against four other low-level-design skills and against the same model with no skill. Full method, raw answers and every judge's scores: evals/benchmark.md.

stories.title: Hard Drive pricing has gotten bad
stories.body: The same 20TB drive went from $249.99 to $549.99 in two Black Fridays. I dug through eight years of receipts, including my ServerPartDeals orders.

views.text: While I see the same issues, it is hard to see how the prices will normalize. It is very difficult for any new entrants to get into this market and compete given the high capital requirements.
views.author: berkeleyjunk

views.text:
Yeah, this mirrors exactly what I have experienced in Australia.

I started a business in 2023-2024 that needs a lot of storage (petabytes) and gosh that's really hurt our ability to sacle things. SSD'd were hit first, so we were a bit ahead of the curve and bought 20 packs of HDD's. That definitely kept us going. But I don't know if we can do more than another year at this kind of pricing.
views.author: memoriesofsmell

views.text:
It really is bad.

I bought 10x18TB drives in 2023 for $190/each, for my 8 bay NAS. 1 started giving smart errors since so was retired, and now I have 1 spare.

Which sounds like I timed things well, but I still need to backup my ever increasing datahoard and I'm having to get very creative reusing old 4TB drives now, making it a very slow process!
views.author: ferrouswheel

discussion.text:
I’m frankly shocked that personal computing has survived this long. The whole concept of the ATX case and having an industry wide standard format for parts we can mix and match is such a clear enemy of the corporations that want a strong say in everything. More than that, it represents real power. That people can wield this kind of technology entirely on their terms.

I think human caricature Sam Altman said the quiet part out loud when he suggested it’s a mistake for us plebs to have RAM at home. A side effect of the AI revolution can be to re-centralize this power.
discussion.author: Waterluvian

discussion.text: Even with black friday these prices for everything is horrible. Any mini pc with 32gb of ram is close to $500. I'm trying to increase my proxmox cluster size and I don't know if I will. The only thing that is alright priced right now are monitors
discussion.author: neko_ranger

discussion.text: All because AI companies walked in like Ron Swanson and said "I want all the CPUs, GPUs, RAM, and storage you have. You might think I meant 'I want a lot of CPUs, GPUs, RAM, and storage'. No... I want all the CPUs, GPUs, RAM, and storage you have."
discussion.author: bitwize

discussion.text: I bought a bunch of hard drives at the end of 2025 anticipating exactly this...
discussion.author: nialv7
